mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 2% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of instances following a triggered INDPRO decline, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, with the 3-month change exceeding 0.5 percentage points, signals a weakening labor market that will drag on consumer spending and weigh on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) continue to grow at an above-trend pace during the signal period, indicating consumer resilience despite rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, indicating the market is not responding to the restrictive policy signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Existing home sales (EXHOSL) decline year-over-year during the signal period, indicating the housing market is not as strong as the HOUST data suggests.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4%, it signals a tight labor market that will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings (AHETPI) growth slows during the signal period, indicating that the tight labor market is not translating into higher wages.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) both decline simultaneously, it signals a unique combination of supply and demand weakness that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of instances when both INDPRO and UNRATE decline, indicating the market is not responding to the combined supply and demand weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both rise simultaneously, it signals a toxic combination of tightening monetary policy and rising inflation that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise, indicating the market is not responding to the toxic combination of tightening and inflation.
